title: Boundary stalk as inertia invariants
statement:
Let $j:U_0\hookrightarrow C_0$ be a dense open immersion of smooth
curves over $k_0$, let $\mathcal F$ be lisse on $U_0$, and let
$x\in C_0\setminus U_0$ be a closed boundary point with local residue
field $\kappa(x)$ and inertia group $I_x$ of [d-real-boundary] inside the local
fundamental group of the
fundamental representation.
Then the boundary stalk of the
middle extension is

$$
(j_*\mathcal F)_{\bar x}\simeq\mathcal F_{\bar\eta}^{I_x},
$$

where $\mathcal F_{\bar\eta}$ is the
geometric generic stalk of
$\mathcal F$ at $x$ and the invariants are formed for the inertia
action. The identification is equivariant for Frobenius: the geometric
Frobenius of $\kappa(x)$ acting on the stalk of the Weil sheaf
$j_*\mathcal F$ at $\bar x$ corresponds to the action of a residue
Frobenius lift on $\mathcal F_{\bar\eta}^{I_x}$ of [d-real-boundary]
(which is independent of the lift).

proof.text:
Put $A=\mathcal O_{C_0,x}$. By [lem-sc-smooth-regular], $A$ is regular and hence Noetherian. The pure dimension-one convention of [def-wf-middle-extension, def-weil-pure-dimension] and the codimension formula of [lem-sc-scheme-stalk-dimension-generalization-chains] give $\dim A=1$: the closed singleton $\{x\}$ is properly contained in an irreducible component of dimension one, so there is a chain of length one, and a longer chain would contradict that component's dimension. Hence [lem-sc-regular-dim1-dvr] makes $A$ a DVR. By [lem-sc-strict-henselization-dvr], $R=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{C_0,\bar x}$ is a DVR and $A\to R$ is injective and local. A DVR has just the primes $(0)$ and its maximal ideal: by [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], a nonzero prime is $(a)$; if $a=bc$, primality and cancellation force one factor to be a unit. Any principal ideal properly containing $(a)$ is therefore the unit ideal, so $(a)$ is maximal. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}R$ has just its generic and closed point. The closed point maps to $x\notin U_0$; the generic point contracts to $(0)$ in $A$, hence maps to the generic point of the component of $C_0$ through $x$, which lies in $U_0$ by density. Base change of the open immersion therefore gives
$$U_0\times_{C_0}\operatorname{Spec}R=\operatorname{Spec}R\setminus\{\mathfrak m_R\}=\operatorname{Spec}\operatorname{Frac}(R).$$

proof.text: Apply [lem-wf-strict-henselian-fraction-inertia] to $A$. With $H=A^{\mathrm h}$, $K_x=\operatorname{Frac}(H)$, $L=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$, a compatible separable closure $\Omega$ of $K_x$ and $D_x=\operatorname{Gal}(\Omega/K_x)$, the residue kernel in $\operatorname{Gal}(\Omega/K_x)$ is precisely $\operatorname{Gal}(\Omega/L)$. This is the group $I_x$ defined as the residue kernel in [d-real-boundary], since the henselization has residue field $\kappa(x)$. There the Galois group is formed with an algebraic closure $\overline K_x\supset\Omega$; restriction $\operatorname{Gal}(\overline K_x/K_x)\to\operatorname{Gal}(\Omega/K_x)$ is an isomorphism: automorphisms preserve the separable elements, one fixing $\Omega$ fixes each $a$ since $a^{p^m}\in\Omega$ has a unique $p^m$-th root, and each automorphism of $\Omega$ extends to its algebraic closure. It respects the residue maps, $\kappa(x)$ being finite hence perfect, so the two residue kernels correspond. Fix the geometric point and path of [d-real-boundary]; they give a homomorphism $\theta_x:D_x\to\pi_1(U_0)$, whose restriction to $W(K_x)$ lands in $W(U_0)$. No injectivity of $\theta_x$ is required. Thus the punctured strict henselian trait in Step 1 is the spectrum of a field with absolute Galois group $I_x$, not the full decomposition group. The same lemma identifies $D_x/I_x$, the automorphisms of $R$ over $H$, and $\operatorname{Gal}(\overline{\kappa(x)}/\kappa(x))$; the residue field is finite here, so its separable closure is its algebraic closure.

source.place: Tag 0BSW (lemma-identify-inertia), specialized to the henselian local fraction field in d-real-boundary

proof.text: Work at the finite coefficient levels $\mathcal F_n$ of a lisse $\mathcal O_E$-model, as in [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves]; these are torsion abelian sheaves. The open immersion $j$ is qcqs (the curves are separated finite-type over a field and hence Noetherian), so the $q=0$ clause of [prop-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-stalk-formula] identifies $(j_*\mathcal F_n)_{\bar x}$ with $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}L,p^{-1}\mathcal F_n)$ by canonical restriction. By [lem-exc-abelian-sheaves-gmodules], this sheaf on the field corresponds to its geometric generic stalk $M_n$ as a discrete $\operatorname{Gal}(\Omega/L)=I_x$-module. Here $M_n=(\mathcal F_n)_{\bar\eta}$: by [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-pullback-stalk](2) both are sections of the inverse image to $\operatorname{Spec}\overline K_x$, and inverse images compose since direct images do. The lift-change action of $\sigma\in I_x$ on these stalks, transported along the fixed path, is the action of $\theta_x(\sigma)$, which [d-real-boundary] defines as path transport of the map of $\operatorname{Spec}K_x\to U_0$, and at finite level [def-wf-fundamental-representation] is evaluation of that fibre-functor automorphism; so the invariants are those of $\rho\circ\theta_x|_{I_x}$. Sections are invariants: $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}L,G)=\operatorname{Hom}(\underline{\mathbf Z},G)$, and the equivalence sends the constant sheaf $\underline{\mathbf Z}$ to $\mathbf Z$ with trivial action, so these morphisms are the equivariant maps $\mathbf Z\to M_n$, determined by an invariant image of $1$. Consequently $(j_*\mathcal F_n)_{\bar x}\simeq M_n^{I_x}$, compatibly in $n$. The finite-level direct-image convention is that of [d-real-boundary, def-wf-middle-extension], and stalks use [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. No finite cover trivializing the rational lisse sheaf is assumed.

proof.text: Write $M=\varprojlim_n M_n$ and $V=M\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$ at the chosen coefficient stage [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves]. The coefficientwise direct-image convention [d-real-boundary] gives the boundary fibre $(\varprojlim_n M_n^{I_x})\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$. A compatible tuple is fixed exactly when each coordinate is fixed, hence $\varprojlim_n M_n^{I_x}=M^{I_x}$. Since $M\subset V$ is an invariant lattice, $M^{I_x}=M\cap V^{I_x}$ is saturated: if $av$ is fixed, $a\ne0$ and $v\in M$, then $a(gv-v)=0$ in the torsion-free $M$, so $v$ is fixed. Conversely each vector in $V^{I_x}$ can be multiplied by a nonzero scalar to lie in $M^{I_x}$. Thus $M^{I_x}\otimes E=V^{I_x}$. Extending from $E$ to $\Qlb$ preserves this equality: in the finite-dimensional $V$, the intersection $\bigcap_{g\in I_x}\ker(g-1)$ equals a finite subintersection (choose one with minimal dimension), and finite kernels commute with field extension by row reduction. This proves the displayed identification in the coefficient convention of the item. The tower $(M_n^{I_x})_n$ need not itself be adic; only its limit is used.

source.place: First paragraph, inverse limit, saturation and rationalization; explicit coordinate and denominator arguments

proof.text: Write $c$ for the restriction comparison of Steps 3-4. For $\sigma\in W(K_x)$, [lem-wf-strict-henselian-fraction-inertia] gives an automorphism of $R$ over $H$ with residue action $\mathrm{res}(\sigma)$. Restriction commutes with it: restricting $\sigma^*s$ is pulling back the restriction of $s$, since both evaluate along the same composite geometric generic point. The field-sheaf equivalence [lem-exc-abelian-sheaves-gmodules] uses exactly this action by changing pointed etale lifts. Restriction is also natural in coefficient morphisms: for $u:\mathcal F_n\to\mathcal G_n$, evaluation gives $c_{\mathcal G_n}(j_*u)_{\bar x}=u_{\bar\eta}c_{\mathcal F_n}$ [def-wf-middle-extension]. This equality passes to limits and scalar extension. For a rational morphism, choose a common finite coefficient field and write $u=a^{-1}v$ with $a\ne0$ and $v$ an integral model morphism [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves]; divide the equality for $v$ by $a$. Thus it applies to Weil descent without requiring a Frobenius-stable lattice. By [def-wf-fundamental-representation], the Weil operator is the composite of the descent map and inverse path transport, $T_s=\varphi_{\bar\eta}L_s^{-1}$; general degrees use the displayed extension formula. Both constituent maps commute with $c$ by the preceding identities. Consequently the residue Weil action on the boundary fibre corresponds to $\rho\circ\theta_x|_{W(K_x)}$ on its inertia invariants [d-real-boundary]. Taking $\sigma$ over geometric Frobenius of $\kappa(x)$ gives the claimed equivariance (its degree over $k_0$ is $[\kappa(x):k_0]$). Two lifts differ by $I_x$ [d-real-boundary], so act equally on invariants. Only local Weil elements act on the rational fibre.
